book.twilightforest_finale.engineering_n: Engineering Notes
An Adherent

The High Priest sent me to help the brothers upstairs. He says I am the only one who has visited "that" world.

I am rather looking forward to it...

I met the figure upstairs. Everyone bowed, so I did too. Mist hid his face, however hard I looked.

His task was strange: teach a heap of stones to obey.

The basement is full of materials from outside the castle: stone, red dust, and strange things sealed in glass.

None of the brothers carrying them knows what they are for.

Following an unsigned drawing, I built an enormous machine. Its arms are wider than my room.

The figure upstairs inspected it. I still do not know what to call him, so I just kept nodding.

First test: a leak. Second test: an explosion. Third test: it finally moved, then caught fire.

The High Priest calls this "progress." I need a sturdier wrench.

I opened the left arm. Three joints were loose. A fourth was not connected at all.

The drawing shows one unbroken line. Whoever drew it has never tightened a bolt.

New joints, same leak. After hours following the pipe, I discovered the pipe beside it was leaking.

I sealed both. At least the floor is dry.

The red-dust circuit in the right arm keeps switching itself on. I isolated it; now nothing moves.

Apparently the machine dislikes both company and silence.

The rear glass cracked. I fitted a thicker pane, but the little cube inside began spinning faster.

It is not decoration. Next time, keep my hands well clear.

The High Priest asked for a trap. "What should it catch?" I asked. "Flying things," he said.

There are many flying things here. I hope he does not mean us.

I fitted the trap backwards. It swallowed every tool on my desk and nearly swallowed me.

There is now an arrow on the inlet. Never install anything by guessing.

Today: the left-arm nozzle. It sprays quite happily, just never forwards.

I turned the whole assembly around. We can finally stop replacing the floor.

Damp red dust refuses to work. I raised the circuit, as they do in "that" world.

The High Priest approved. I did not mention the six failed attempts.

The machine looks one way and walks another. I checked its legs; the fault was in its shoulders.

Both directions now share one shaft. It has stopped circling me.

Its body slides away before its feet move. I added a delay so each foot lands before the next step.

Clumsier, perhaps, but there are fewer holes in the wall.

The ground slam worked. It brought down the ceiling bricks too.

I meant to fix that fault. The figure upstairs signalled that I should leave it. What an odd request.

I added a timer to the nozzle. Three seconds, no longer.

After the last test we could not see the basement door for hours. I refuse to find the exit by feeling along the wall again.

The charged trap made a horrible sustained noise. A new indicator now chimes for each increment of energy.

At last, I can hear the difference.

Someone suggested thinner leg armour so the machine could walk faster.

I refused. Repairing a leg is difficult enough. Repairing a brother it has stepped on would be worse.

The left arm lost support and the machine sat down. I replaced a scorched connector. Five seconds later, it stood up.

Remember that recovery time.

I added a backup circuit. When one wire breaks, the other takes over.

Now the fault is harder to find. "Still running" and "repaired" are apparently different things.

The rear glass must sit inside the body. A protruding corner caught the wall yesterday.

I carved a proper recess. The little cube can spin without hitting anything.

Another broken wrench. I made a replacement from the dark violet material.

Surprisingly light. It throws well too, though I still have to fetch it afterwards.

Three consecutive slam tests. The first was good. So was the second. The third destroyed the recording desk.

The recorder must stand farther away. Preferably, I must stand farther away.

I fixed the conflicting arm commands. The left arm cannot reach out while it is supporting the right.

One sentence to describe the fault. Three days to find it.

I numbered every joint and labelled every wire.

The High Priest said it looked undignified. I moved the labels to the back. I hope dignity will not get in the way of repairs.

Another bang in the basement at night. I rushed down with my wrench. The trap had merely snapped shut too hard.

I added a buffer. Perhaps tonight I can sleep.

Today we tried fire, explosions, and flying weapons. The shell endured them all.

The brothers say nothing can hurt it. I am keeping my tools nearby. People say such things too soon.

I checked every pipe again. No leaks, loose joints, or trembling glass.

To make certain I was not imagining it, I watched the machine for an entire day.

The final overhaul is done. It walks, stops, and follows the right commands.

The figure upstairs finally nodded. The High Priest says one last test remains, and only I can perform it.

Repaired. It really seems fearless, but that is precisely why I was summoned.

I immediately recognised something from "that" world. Contact damages the mechanism. I am recording this separately.

I built another machine in the basement. Perhaps it can avoid that flaw. Unfinished, yet already working; progress feels almost too quick.

I made a barrier for the figure upstairs. Work can begin soon.

The High Priest says I have done splendidly. He will retire soon. Perhaps I shall be the next High Priest!

A happy day. But why has an enormous tree grown beneath the neighbouring cloud?

No audiences. No new orders. Even the basement has fallen silent. Those barriers did not break themselves.

Now I know something terrible happened. Pack this journal. Do not look back. I am leaving.

An explosion came from the basement. The new machine passed every test. That sound should not have happened.

Perhaps someone touched the wrong switch. I shall take my wrench and ask the High Priest.

The High Priest says I shall succeed him very soon. It must be the wish of the figure upstairs.

There is a noise below. Perhaps the brothers bring good news. I shall have a look.

The High Priest says my appointment is near, yet the new basement machine has failed. No fresh orders from upstairs either.

Another sound below. I shall investigate, then report to the High Priest.

The castle has grown quiet. No audience with the High Priest for days. Even the barrier I made for the figure upstairs has somehow broken.

Enough guessing. I shall go and see the High Priest myself.

They say something happened to the High Priest. Impossible. He was directing castle business only yesterday.

It must be a rumour. At my next audience, I shall tell him exactly what they have been saying.

The basement machine is ruined, and the High Priest will not answer. Those rumours... could they be true?

No more waiting. I must arrange more barriers and protect the entire castle.
twilightforest.book.castle.1:
§8[[An explorer's notebook, sealed by magic]]§0

I have used every ounce of my strength to break through the blockade of acid rain and the high wall of thorns. What greets my eyes is a giant, pristine castle standing upon the grey highlands—sacred, majestic, and mysterious. I hope I can find what I seek within its walls.
twilightforest.book.castle.2:
As I stepped into the castle, I could feel an intense surge of magical aura. It seems this is indeed the very purpose of my journey.

§8[[Next entry]]§0

There are four locations within the castle that emanate an eerie, unsettling aura. One is the soaring clock tower adjacent to the castle; another is the highest spire of the castle's main tower; the third lies in the deepest depths of the castle basement; and the last—by far the most terrifying—is the force field at the very center of the castle. Something extraordinary seems to be sealed within it.
twilightforest.book.castle.3:
§8[[Many entries later]]§0

The combination of the acid rain and the castle's sheer magical power has left my entire body numb. Lacking any items to counter these malevolent influences, I fear my time is running short. Yet, I harbor no regrets. I can only hope that someone will discover these notes, inherit my will, and save this forest...
twilightforest.book.castle.4: §8[[The notes come to an abrupt end]]§0
